label: copy-phase input token x (from the 2nd copied token on)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input token is x, i.e. the model just emitted an x and is now outputting the token after it. Zero activation in the original phase and at the delimiter, and never on any other input token. At recall_idx >= 2 it fires on every such step (dev precision 1.0). When x is the first copied token (input at recall_idx 1, i.e. orig(0) == x) it fires only weakly and rarely (about 1752 dev activations, in the lowest quartile). In the examples, magnitude is higher for x later in the copy sequence (top activations around 0.95-1.0 of max) than for early positions (lowest-quartile examples are mostly x at copy position 1-2). Output token, L, and digit content have no clear effect.

issues: None of the claims are refuted. On test the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 0.976, F1 0.988 and mass recall 0.999, with 0 false positives.

Every one of the 1797 test misses has in_tok x at recall_idx 1 (orig(0)==x), with activation around 0.01-0.05 of max. Together they hold 0.1% of the activation mass. This matches the explanation's description of rare, weak firing there, so it is not a new class of counterexample.
The profile confirms zero activations in the original phase, at the delimiter and on any input token other than x.

The magnitude claim holds, but it is stated vaguely. Mean activation per active step (mass share divided by active count) is about 1.05e-5 at recall_idx 2 and about 1.4e-5 from recall_idx 3 onward. So activation rises once and then stays flat; it does not keep growing with copy position.
